bls-census.name: bls-census
bls-census.description: Free labor-force, demographic, and earnings panels from the BLS public data API (LFPR, employment, payrolls, CPI/PPI — no key needed), Census ACS5 / basic-monthly CPS (county demographics and CPS person extracts — free key required), and SSA OACT period life tables. Zero overlap with WRDS/CRSP. Use for shift-share / Bartik instruments (cohort aging, local labor demand, retirement-channel shifters), labor-finance, household-finance, and macro-cross-section work.

claude.argument-hint: [BLS series ID, ACS variable, or description]

call-reports.name: call-reports
call-reports.description: Quarterly bank balance sheets / income statements without WRDS's bank library or S&P CIQ. Three free no-key sources, each with a different ID: (1) FFIEC CDR bulk SDF — literal RCON/RIAD-coded Call Reports for every FDIC-insured bank, keyed by IDRSSD, scraped from the ASP.NET bulk-download form (the documented free path, brittle by design); (2) FR Y-9C BHCF flat files — consolidated bank-holding-company statements, BHCK-coded, keyed by RSSD9001 (Chicago Fed 1986Q1-2021Q1 live, NIC user-placed for 2021Q2+); (3) FDIC Financial Data API — robust standardized (non-RCON) panel keyed by CERT, the reliable fallback and the bidirectional RSSD/CERT crosswalk. Use for the banking / monetary-transmission / intermediary-asset-pricing channel: bank lending, deposits, liquidity regulation, CET1 capital, NIM.

claude.argument-hint: [quarter e.g. 2023Q4, RSSD/CERT id, or RCON code]

canonical-packages.name: canonical-packages
canonical-packages.description: Policy + procedure for not reimplementing econometric methods that have canonical, author-maintained packages. Field-tier finance referees (JF/JFE/RFS) reject custom code that re-derives well-known estimators (HonestDiD, Sensemakr, Callaway-Sant'Anna, wild cluster bootstrap, etc.) — see GitHub issue #36. This skill does NOT catalog packages; it tells you when to look one up (before writing code for any named econometric method), where to look (method author's site, PyPI, CRAN, Stata SSC, WebSearch), and how to document a legitimate deviation via the (a)–(d) justification taxonomy. The actual canonical-package discovery is done on demand by the empiricist (before coding) and by the `method-checker` agent (during audit at Stage 3a step 7.5) using PyPI / CRAN / SSC queries plus training knowledge.

chen-zimmerman.name: chen-zimmerman
chen-zimmerman.description: Open Source Asset Pricing dataset (Chen & Zimmerman 2022). 212 firm-level anomaly signals with portfolio returns. Use for cross-sectional calibration, testing anomaly predictions, and constructing characteristic-sorted portfolios.

tnic.name: tnic
tnic.description: Hoberg-Phillips Text-based Network Industry Classifications (TNIC) — pairwise product-market similarity from 10-K product descriptions, no key/registration. Direct download from hobergphillips.tuck.dartmouth.edu: tnic3_data.zip (~151 MB; tab-delimited year/gvkey1/gvkey2/score, 27M rows, 1988-2023; recommended), plus coarser TNIC-2 and the transitive FIC classification. Use for text-based industry/peer definitions, product-market competition intensity, peer-firm benchmarks, and merger/synergy work. Gotchas: it is a non-transitive network with no industry code (each firm has its own rival set), not a partition like SIC/NAICS; identifier is Compustat gvkey; score is excess-over-threshold not raw cosine; symmetric (both directions stored, deduplicate by keeping gvkey1 below gvkey2); self-pairs present; recomputed annually. Cite Hoberg & Phillips RFS 2010 and JPE 2016.

facebook-sci.name: facebook-sci
facebook-sci.description: Meta (Facebook) Social Connectedness Index (SCI) via the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX) — relative probability of a friendship link between two areas, no API key. Direct CSVs: country.csv (country-to-country, 31,684 rows) and us_counties.csv (~245 MB, 10.3M rows, 5-digit FIPS); GADM2/ZCTA files are Google Drive links on the same page. Columns: user_country, friend_country, user_region, friend_region, scaled_sci. Use for social-network exposure measures, social-distance instruments, and connectedness-weighted spillovers. Gotchas: scaled_sci is a per-file rescaled relative measure (max=1e9), NOT a count/probability and NOT comparable across files or vintages; symmetric (both directions stored); diagonal (self-pairs) included and dominates — drop for between-area work; region codes differ by file; snapshot per release, not a panel. Cite Bailey, Cao, Kuchler, Stroebel & Wong, JEP 2018.

paris-club.name: paris-club
paris-club.description: Paris Club Dataset (1956-2026; van der Zaag, van Mourik & Blackmon) — agreement-level record of every sovereign debt restructuring negotiated through the Paris Club of official bilateral creditors, no key, CC BY 4.0. One zip from Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/BBWLO8, ~2.3 MB): 543 agreements, 102 debtors, 1956 to 2024-08, in tabular (one row per agreement), long, network (creditor/observer edges) and xlsx layouts. Fields: debtor, participating creditors, amounts treated/cancelled/rescheduled, terms (Toronto/London/Naples/Lyon/Cologne/HIPC Exit, plus the Houston track), cut-off dates, meeting chairs, observers, source URLs. Use for sovereign default, official debt relief, and DSSI work. Gotchas: the published USD 863bn total is inflated by a x100 decimal-comma bug on 41 DSSI rows (USD 609bn once repaired; this skill ships the fix); cancelled is populated for only 84 of 543; no unique key (DSSI extensions share a url); country names are free text, no ISO codes; excludes China and private restructurings.

open-bond-pricing.name: open-bond-pricing
open-bond-pricing.description: Open Source Bond Asset Pricing (OSBAP; Dickerson, Nozawa & Robotti) — corporate-bond data with NO WRDS and NO authentication, the fixed-income analog of chen-zimmerman. Public downloads, cached locally: ~341 long-short corporate-bond factor return series (monthly from 2002-08, ~2 MB); the bond-month characteristics panel of 341 ranked predictors (2002-07..2022-12, ~886 MB); ML return predictions + realized returns (~200 MB); and a daily bond panel from cleaned Enhanced/Standard/144A TRACE with returns, credit spreads, duration and accrued interest (~1.8 GB). OSBAP already cleans raw TRACE (error-correction, +100% truncation fix) so you consume the panels rather than re-clean trades. Use for corporate-bond cross-section, credit-spread, bond-factor, and bond-return work. Trade-level intraday TRACE (individual trade reports / dealer flow via a WRDS trace-library, subscription-gated pull) is the separate `trace-bonds` skill, not this one.

trace-bonds.name: trace-bonds
trace-bonds.description: Trade-level FINRA TRACE corporate-bond transactions via WRDS — the subscription-gated complement to open-bond-pricing (issue #8 Tier 2). Pulls individual trade reports (cusip, execution date/time, clean price, par volume, yield, buy/sell side, customer/dealer counterparty) from the trace.* library, auto-preferring the cleaned wrdsapps_bondret.* tables when the account has them. Helpers: trace_available() (probe which sources this account can read — TRACE is NOT in every subscription), trace_trades() (filtered trade pull), bond_daily_panel() (volume-weighted daily price/yield by bond-day), dealer_inventory_proxy() (signed customer flow = dealer inventory change, customer-side only so no inter-dealer double count), link_bond_to_crsp() (CUSIP to permno/permco). Applies only a light trc_st='T' keep filter, NOT full Dick-Nielsen error-correction — for analysis-ready returns/characteristics use the self-contained open-bond-pricing skill instead. Requires WRDS_USER/WRDS_PASS and the persistent WRDS server (Duo 2FA once per session).

codex.description: Trade-level FINRA TRACE corporate-bond transactions via WRDS (trace.* / wrdsapps_bondret.*) — the subscription-gated complement to open-bond-pricing. Pulls individual trade reports (cusip, execution date/time, clean price, par volume, yield, buy/sell side, counterparty). Helpers: trace_available() (probe entitlement — TRACE is NOT in every subscription), trace_trades() (filtered pull), bond_daily_panel() (volume-weighted daily price/yield by bond-day), dealer_inventory_proxy() (signed customer flow), link_bond_to_crsp() (CUSIP to permno/permco). Applies only a light trc_st='T' keep filter, NOT full Dick-Nielsen error-correction — for analysis-ready returns/characteristics use the open-bond-pricing skill instead. Requires WRDS_USER/WRDS_PASS and the persistent WRDS server (Duo 2FA once per session).

ibes.name: ibes
ibes.description: I/B/E/S analyst EPS estimates, consensus summaries, and Street actuals via WRDS. Prefer unadjusted statsumu_epsus/detu_epsus/actu_epsus, then align split bases with CRSP cfacshr. Forecast-error joins must match measure, FPI-to-pdicity, currency, and a deliberate Summary estflag; Detail revisions follow announce/activation timestamps, while revdats/revtims are confirmations and pdf records received P/D provenance. Link ticker to CRSP through date-bounded wrdsapps.ibcrsphist/ICLINK with score at most 2, not ibes.id or a naive CUSIP merge. Covers Summary-vs-Detail, Street-vs-GAAP, vintage/restatement, US-vs-international, dispersion, surprise, and revision gotchas. Requires WRDS_USER/WRDS_PASS and the persistent WRDS server; reuse the wrds skill's connection.

codex.description: I/B/E/S analyst EPS estimates, consensus summaries, and Street actuals via WRDS. Prefer unadjusted statsumu_epsus/detu_epsus/actu_epsus and align split bases with CRSP cfacshr. Match measure, FPI-to-pdicity, currency, and Summary estflag; order Detail revisions by announce/activation timestamps because revdats/revtims are confirmations and pdf is received P/D provenance. Link to CRSP through date-bounded wrdsapps.ibcrsphist/ICLINK with score at most 2, not ibes.id or CUSIP. Covers Summary-vs-Detail, Street-vs-GAAP, vintage, dispersion, surprise, and revisions. Requires the persistent WRDS server.

edgar.name: edgar
edgar.description: Access SEC EDGAR filings, financial statements, and full-text search. Use for corporate finance research — 10-K/10-Q analysis, governance, disclosure, insider trading, institutional holdings, and open-end fund registration (Form N-1A: mutual fund / ETF prospectus, strategy, fees, classification — rr:* XBRL not us-gaap, one trust covers many series/classes). For investment-adviser registration (CRD/IARD, not on EDGAR) see form-adv; for N-CEN/NPORT-P/485BPOS fee-table parsing see sec-funds.

form-adv.name: form-adv
form-adv.description: SEC Form ADV via IAPD (Investment Adviser Public Disclosure) — free, public, no API key. Registration form every SEC- or state-registered investment adviser files. NOT on EDGAR: uses CRD/IARD identifiers (CRD numbers, 801-/802- file numbers), not CIK. Three access paths: the IAPD firm-report PDF (reports.adviserinfo.sec.gov/reports/ADV/{CRD}/PDF/{CRD}.pdf), the firm/individual search API (resolve name→CRD), and the SEC FOIA bulk structured Part 1 filing-data zips for population-scale panels. Use for classifying advisers/funds (hedge-fund vs mutual-fund adviser, private-fund flags via Schedule D 7.B.1), adviser AUM and client/employee counts, ownership, and disciplinary history. Gotchas: AUM is regulated AUM (RAUM, gross, not net); SEC vs state vs exempt-reporting-adviser regimes differ in coverage; Part 2 brochure is prose, not fields; bulk filenames embed date ranges. Join to EDGAR-based 13-F / N-1A holdings via a hand-built CRD↔CIK crosswalk (no shared key) — use the edgar skill for the holdings side.

NOT on EDGAR: uses CRD/IARD identifiers (CRD numbers, 801-/802- file numbers), not CIK. Three access paths: the IAPD firm-report PDF (reports.adviserinfo.sec.gov/reports/ADV/{CRD}/PDF/{CRD}.pdf), the firm/individual search API (resolve name to CRD), and the SEC FOIA bulk structured Part 1 filing-data zips for population-scale panels. Gotchas: AUM is regulated AUM (RAUM, gross, not net); SEC vs state vs exempt-reporting-adviser regimes differ in coverage; Part 2 brochure is prose, not fields. Join to EDGAR-based 13-F / N-1A holdings via a hand-built CRD-CIK crosswalk (no shared key) — use the edgar skill for the holdings side.

flex-mining.name: flex-mining
flex-mining.description: Flexible data mining strategies from Chen, Lopez-Lira & Zimmermann. 30,000+ long-short trading strategies from CRSP/Compustat ratios. Use for benchmarking published predictors against data-mined alternatives, testing sufficiency of published literature, and studying the cross-section of expected returns.

form-5500.name: form-5500
form-5500.description: DOL EBSA Form 5500 — annual ERISA filings for every U.S. pension/welfare plan with ≥100 participants. Schedule H gives plan-level asset breakdowns including mutual-fund holdings (INT_REG_INVST_CO_*_AMT); Schedule R covers retirement-plan distributions and rollovers. Free public-use research files. Use for retirement, household finance, defined-contribution/401(k), and labor-finance research.

fred.name: fred
fred.description: Fetch macroeconomic and financial time series from FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data). Use when calibrating models to macro moments, testing time-series predictions, or getting risk-free rates, spreads, and macro indicators.

hrs-scf.name: hrs-scf
hrs-scf.description: Household-survey panels for retirement, wealth, and household balance sheets. SCF (Survey of Consumer Finances, Federal Reserve, triennial 1989–2022) downloads with NO key — Summary Extract and Full Public Data Set with 5 multiply-imputed implicates. HRS (Health & Retirement Study / RAND HRS Longitudinal File) is registration-walled: the helper reads a user-placed extract from data/hrs_scf/hrs/ (the realistic workflow — bulk download after accepting the data-use agreement) and documents the registration step; it never fails silently. Use for retirement timing, IRA/401(k) balances by cohort, wealth distribution, and household-finance micro-validation (e.g. pairing HRS individual retirement timing with macro Bartik shifters). Rollover/pension-disposition events need HRS detailed-pension stems supplied via stems= (documented, not the default panel).

claude.argument-hint: [SCF year, RAND HRS variable, or description]

ken-french.name: ken-french
ken-french.description: Download factor returns, portfolio returns, and breakpoints from the Ken French Data Library. Use for asset pricing calibration, computing alphas, and building test assets.

mutual-funds.name: mutual-funds
mutual-funds.description: CRSP Mutual Fund Database + Thomson Reuters holdings via WRDS. Fund returns, NAV, TNA, fees, flows, holdings, and style classifications. Use for mutual fund performance, flow-performance, holdings-based analysis, and fund manager skill.

ravenpack.name: ravenpack
ravenpack.description: RavenPack News Analytics (LICENSED — paid subscription, no free tier; access path documented but NOT exercised here, no provenance badge). Converts unstructured news into structured timestamped entity-event records with sentiment, relevance, and novelty scores plus a topic taxonomy. Access direct from the vendor (flat-file dumps + feed) or via WRDS where licensed. Use for news-based signals: event studies, attention/sentiment measures, mapping stories to tickers. Gotchas: filter on RELEVANCE first; deduplicate echoes with the Event Novelty Score (ENS); timestamps are UTC (align to trading calendar and use point-in-time to avoid look-ahead); sentiment scales differ between RavenPack 1.0 and later editions; records key on RP_ENTITY_ID, not ticker/PERMNO (entity mapping is its own step).

factset-lionshares.name: factset-lionshares
factset-lionshares.description: FactSet LionShares / FactSet Ownership (LICENSED — paid subscription, no free tier; access path documented but NOT exercised here, no provenance badge). Position-level panel of global institutional and fund equity holdings assembled from 13-F and equivalents and fund disclosures, with each holder classified by type (mutual fund, hedge fund, pension, bank, insurance). Access direct from FactSet or via WRDS where licensed. Use for ownership / institutional-investor work needing holdings plus a holder-type split. Gotchas: holdings are stale between report dates (carried forward, not live); 13-F reports lag up to 45 days and confidential-treatment requests omit positions; institution vs fund level can double-count — pick one; holder classification has edge cases (multi-strategy, manager changes); identifiers are FactSet's own (build a crosswalk to PERMNO/CIK); non-US coverage is sparser than US 13-F.

revelio.name: revelio
revelio.description: Revelio Labs workforce / human-capital panel via WRDS schema revelio (LICENSED commercial source; confirmed live on this entitlement 2026-06-27, queried through the persistent WRDS server like crsp.*). Firm-level panel from aggregated public professional profiles and job postings: headcount (realized stock via individual_positions), hiring flow (postings_cosmos, ~2.6B rows 2008-present), role/seniority mix, skills (AI/ML talent share), layoffs, inferred compensation, and employer sentiment (incl. innovative_technology_sentiment). Keyed on rcid; company_mapping bridges rcid to gvkey/cusip/cik/ticker (only ~65k of 32.7M rcids carry a gvkey, so filter to the listed universe). Use for labor / human-capital channels: workforce composition, hiring dynamics, skill mix, layoffs. Gotchas: backfill/look-ahead is the #1 hazard for return-prediction (history is restated from profiles scraped now — enforce point-in-time via post_date/startdate/first_reported and a pinned vintage); levels are estimates skewed white-collar/US/large (prefer within-firm changes, use the weight column not row counts); profiles self-reported/inferred; panels restated across vintages (pin the pull date); entity mapping is its own step (rcid vs ultimate_parent_rcid); the billion-row tables time out unfiltered (always constrain by rcid list + date range). Still licensed — cite the vendor, not a free/public badge.

Licensed — cite the vendor, not a free/public badge.

sec-funds.name: sec-funds
sec-funds.description: Parse SEC fund-specific filings from EDGAR — N-CEN (annual census: advisers, underwriters, securities lending, expense waivers), NPORT-P (monthly portfolio holdings), and N-1A/485BPOS Risk/Return XBRL (per-share-class fee tables: management fee, 12b-1, gross/net expense ratio). Free path to mutual-fund fees/holdings without CRSP. Use for mutual-fund fee, retirement/DC-channel, and holdings-based research.

treasury-yields.name: treasury-yields
treasury-yields.description: Daily zero-coupon Treasury yield curves, NO WRDS, NO auth — the gap left by FRED's par-yield-only coverage (DGS10 et al.). Three sources: (1) GSW nominal (Gürkaynak-Sack-Wright 2007, Fed FEDS 200628) — daily 1961+, Svensson 1980+ / Nelson-Siegel pre-1980, ships fitted parameters BETA0-3/TAU1-2 plus implied zero yields SVENY01-30, par SVENPY01-30, forwards SVENF/SVEN1F; (2) GSW TIPS real curve + breakeven inflation (GSW 2008, FEDS 200805) — daily 1999+, TIPSY/TIPSPY/TIPSF panels plus TIPS5F5 5y5y-forward; (3) Liu-Wu (JFE 2021) — daily and monthly nominal zeros 1961-2025, cubic-spline alternative to GSW for robustness checks. Helpers: gsw_nominal()/gsw_tips() return the full panel; liu_wu(freq) reads the Google-Sheets export; yield_on(date, maturity, source) does scalar lookup with integer fast path and Svensson closed-form for continuous maturity; ns_factors() returns published BETA0-3/TAU1-2 without refitting (BETA0 ≈ level, BETA1 ≈ -slope, BETA2 ≈ curvature). Use for term-structure, monetary-policy-surprise, duration-matched discounting, and real-rate/inflation-expectation work.

wrds.name: wrds
wrds.description: Query WRDS (Wharton Research Data Services) for CRSP, Compustat, IBES, options, insider trading, and other financial databases. Use for firm-level stock returns, accounting data, analyst forecasts, and cross-sectional/panel analysis.

capital-iq.name: capital-iq
capital-iq.description: S&P Capital IQ (CIQ) earnings-call TRANSCRIPTS for firm-level textual measures (tone, topic, disclosure timing), linked to Compustat via gvkey. LICENSED and entitlement-gated: the full ciq / ciq_transcripts WRDS schemas are NOT on the default pipeline entitlement (live check returns permission denied; only ciqsamp_* samples read), so by default you cannot pull CIQ here. Working path = an OPERATOR-SUPPLIED pre-built transcript export taken as given in data/transcripts/ (component-level: gvkey, year, transcriptid, componentorder, transcriptpersonid, componenttext, mostimportantdateutc; standard export = earnings calls keydeveventtypeid=48, deduped earliest per gvkey x call-date, operator turns transcriptpersonid=1 dropped). Provenance recipe (entitled accounts only): ciq.wrds_transcript_detail metadata join ciq_transcripts.ciqtranscriptcomponent text. Gotchas: component grain != call grain (aggregate per transcriptid); export is tens of GB (filter to gvkey set + date window, cache to parquet, never read the whole file); gvkey is the link; licensed (no provenance badge, cite S&P Capital IQ, never commit the data or a download link). If the file is absent the transcript leg is unavailable -- report it, do not attempt an unentitled WRDS pull.

deepvest.name: deepvest
deepvest.description: DeepVest AI research terminal via its remote MCP server (api.deepvest.ai/mcp) — METERED (1,000 free credits/month, then $0.025/credit; ~7–16 credits per call) and LLM-MEDIATED (natural-language `query` tools answered by a vendor-side model; no PERMNO/gvkey, no documented upstream feed, no provenance badge). Access verified live. Use for what WRDS lacks or when WRDS is unavailable: price/return history and fundamentals by ticker (quick_analysis/asset_analysis with format="json"), ETF fund flows + holdings, dividend payment records (dividend_history, typed), ticker screens with `as of` snapshots (stock_screener), options analytics/chains/screens, earnings transcripts + surprises, 13F/N-PORT/XBRL via EDGAR (expensive), macro series (prefer fred). Helper code/utils/deepvest_utils.py: stdlib MCP client, CLI (ping/tools/query/call/cache), per-(tool,arguments) JSON cache under data/deepvest/ as the provenance record, parse_result/tables_from_response for the JSON envelope. Gotchas: ask for raw tables not analysis; price basis unstated (adjusted close observed); current-ticker universe (survivorship); not byte-reproducible across calls; dividend_history caps 60 events/symbol; 20 req/min; fetch BEFORE the results-pipeline run (producer workspace has no DEEPVEST_API_KEY); never report DeepVest backtests/optimizations as results. Requires DEEPVEST_API_KEY in .env.
